What it measures: Local control-flow behaviour: activity pairs and short activity sequences
Change used to validate it: Make parallel activities sequential; change activity order; change gateway probabilities
What the final results show: NGD increases when activity ordering or path frequencies differ from the baseline

What it measures: Full control-flow traces: complete activity sequences of cases
Change used to validate it: Make parallel activities sequential; change gateway probabilities
What the final results show: CFLD increases when complete case traces differ from the baseline; it produced a similar ranking to NGD but is more computationally expensive

What it measures: Global distribution of all event starts and ends over the complete calendar timeline
Change used to validate it: Change case arrival rate; changes that create delays can also affect it
What the final results show: AED increases when the overall distribution of events across time differs from baseline; it identifies a global timing problem but not its exact cause

What it measures: Distribution of events by weekday and hour of day
Change used to validate it: Shift resource working hours, for example 09:00–17:00 → 14:00–22:00
What the final results show: CED strongly increases when events move from morning to afternoon/evening; it is mainly sensitive to working calendars, not resource count

What it measures: Timing of events relative to the beginning of each case
Change used to validate it: Increase activity durations; add timer delays; reduce resource capacity; sequentialise parallel tasks
What the final results show: RED increases when activities occur later within a case because of longer processing, queueing, waiting, or sequential execution

What it measures: Number of active resources by weekday and hour
Change used to validate it: Increase/decrease resource capacity; shift resource working schedules
What the final results show: CWD increases when the number of active resources changes or when their working hours change; this is the main resource-count measure

What it measures: Distribution and frequency of new case arrivals over time
Change used to validate it: Change inter-arrival time or case arrival rate
What the final results show: CAR increases when cases arrive more or less frequently, or at different calendar times, than in the baseline

Change used to validate it: Increase activity durations; add timer delays; reduce resource capacity
What the final results show: CTD increases when cases take longer or shorter to complete because of processing time changes, waiting time, or queueing
